SR-001.justification: 10,000 generated byte strings either decode back exactly with a strict decoder or are refused with the stated reason. A subtree named with quote, backslash and parentheses lowers to exactly one subtree rule that decodes to the name, with no syntax outside the quotes. Newline and non-UTF-8 paths give Unrepresentable gaps on macOS. The quote fuzz target ran 12.7M executions without a crash, and injecting a missing quote escape fails two tests.

SR-002.justification: A subtree containing * ? [ ] stays a subpath and is never a regex. /work/**/*.rs lowers to the anchored pattern with the dot escaped. For 10,000 generated globs an independent check confirms every literal is escaped. [ and { are refused. The glob fuzz target ran 5.9M executions, and injecting an unescaped dot fails two tests.

SR-003.justification: Each of relative, ~, .., ., //, trailing slash and NUL is refused with its typed reason. Non-UTF-8 bytes are kept exactly. 10,000 generated inputs match an independent statement of the rules, and injecting acceptance of .. fails two tests.

SR-004.justification: Operation names with a parenthesis, space or quote, and the name default, are refused when built and when read from a document. Grant names with a quote, space or slash are refused. The raw rule type has no modifier field, and every reference profile contains no (with ...) except the tag. All 112 operations of the closed list compile through libsandbox on macOS 26.6.2.

SR-005.justification: Protect, glob and loopback on T2 return all three typed gaps, sorted, and no plan. An allowed literal approximation gives exactly one recorded degradation, while an unsupported construct stays a gap even when allowed. T2 at ABI 3 and T1 at ABI 0 return LandlockTooOld, and a returned plan names the requested tier.

SR-006.justification: The test parses the rustdoc lowering table and lowers each of the 32 constructs for macOS, T1 and T2 at several ABIs. It asserts the exact, approximated, unsupported or n/a semantics with and without permission. Changing the fs-protect T2 cell fails the test.

SR-007.justification: 50 shuffles of every reference policy give identical plans on 13 targets. No allow follows a deny, and the hard-deny tier is last. A raw allow lands before protect and the tier. Each waiver removes exactly its class's rules and is listed. Moving the tier before deny-within-allow fails the test.

SR-008.justification: A reference last-match-wins evaluator gives identical decisions for 10,000 generated rule lists × 8 requests before and after merge_adjacent. Injecting a merge that ignores the effect fails both tests.

SR-009.justification: 2,001 rules that cannot merge give LimitExceeded naming limit 2000 and the count, and configured limits are honoured. A path whose quoted form is just over 1016 bytes is emitted as (param "P0"), with its exact value in the plan, and libsandbox compiles it only when the parameter is supplied.

SR-010.justification: Unknown fields at the top level, in FsRule and in a struct variant are refused, naming the field. Relative paths, bad globs, unknown classes and operations, and invalid grant names and ports give the constructor's error. Versions other than 1 are refused. 10,000 mutated documents never panic, and the accepted ones round-trip. The format and lower fuzz targets each ran 60 s (5.0M and 378k executions) without a crash.

SR-011.justification: I reviewed the crate docs, the lowering table and the compile test, and recorded the review in the quickstart (scenario 11). The docs state what lowering produces, and that a plan says nothing about enforcement until procage cages a real child. The compile test is labelled well-formedness only. A scan for enforce, protects, prevents, blocks and guarantee finds only these disclaimers.
